classification.difficultyReason: Devise an unsignposted rejection-and-repeat procedure that converts four equally likely two-toss outcomes into three equally likely selections.

content.prompt: Describe how you can use a coin to decide between three menu items with equal probability.

answer.short:
Toss a fair coin twice: HH selects item 1, HT selects item 2, TH selects item 3, and TT means repeat both tosses.

The three accepted outcomes are equally likely.
answer.worked: Use a fair coin and toss it twice. The four equally likely outcomes are HH, HT, TH and TT. Assign HH to item 1, HT to item 2 and TH to item 3. If TT occurs, repeat the two-toss trial until an item is selected. Each accepted outcome has the same chance on every trial, so the three menu items have equal probability $\frac{1}{3}$.
